messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a sudden spike in pod connection drops across eastus3 GPU pool, started ~09:02 UTC. Service healthchecks failing with connection reset. :eyes:

devin: Which nodes? any commonalities (AZ, kernel, CNI)?

maria: Mostly nodes gpu-node-12..16 and gpu-node-21. CPU/mem fine. Networking counters look suspicious. Dumping conntrack on gpu-node-14:
```
$ cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
98012
$ cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
100000
```
Connections stuck in TIME_WAIT/SYN_RECV and a lot of short-lived SNAT entries.

chris: That’s basically natted ephemeral port exhaustion -> new outbound connections start failing. If nf_conntrack is at max packets get dropped/conn reset.

sara: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/_conntrack/conntrack?orgId=1&var-region=eastus3 shows sharp rise starting ~08:58. Pod-level egress spike lines up with model-prefetch cron jobs hitting backend replicas.

alex: Quick mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max and reduce established timeout for TCP to free entries faster. Example: 
```sh
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```
But do with caution — memory usage will rise. Suggest rolling DaemonSet to apply to nodes.

maria: Trying on one node now (gpu-node-14). Also seeing lots of fragmented packets in dmesg: "fragmented packet but no buffer" and MTU errors. We recently enabled RDMA offload on this rack — could be MTU mismatch between host NICs and overlay.

devin: Ah — RDMA/Jumbo frames + overlay without MTU adjust = fragmentation which increases conntrack churn (each fragment tracked until reassembly times out). Check CNI MTU and host MTU: `ip link show` and CNI config.

chris: Commands to check: 
```sh
ip -s link show dev eth0
ethtool -k eth0
cat /etc/cni/net.d/10-calico.conflist | jq '.plugins[].mtu'
```
If host MTU 9000 but overlay set to 1500, fragmentation happens.

sara: We also saw a sudden rise in inter-pod short TCP connections from the model prefetcher (each shard opens fresh connection per file). Short-lived high concurrency + SNAT = many ephemeral ports consumed. Long-term fix: connection pooling or use nodePort/local service mesh to avoid SNAT.

maria: After bumping nf_conntrack_max on gpu-node-14 counts dropped errors for that node, but others are still saturated. Rolling a DaemonSet that sets sysctls now. Deploy-bot: can we patch node bootstrap to include higher conntrack max for eastus3?

deploy-bot: Created rollout run #4572 to push sysctl-daemonset to eastus3 nodes. Staged to 2 nodes for canary.

devin: Action items:
- Short term: DaemonSet to increase nf_conntrack_max to 262144 and lower established timeout to 300s (canary now).
- Short term: throttle model-prefetch concurrency (sara to open PR to change cron to stagger).
- Medium term: audit CNI MTU + RDMA config across the fleet and ensure overlay MTU matches host (+/- overhead).
- Medium term: evaluate eBPF kube-proxy (Cilium) to reduce conntrack reliance, or switch kube-proxy ipvs mode.
- Long term: add per-pod connection pooling lib or sidecar to reduce ephemeral churn.

alex: Also add conntrack metrics alert with two-stage threshold: (1) warn at 70% nf_conntrack_max for >5m, (2) critical at 90% >1m. Current alerting only triggers at 95% which is too late.

maria: Noted. Opening incident ticket now and adding node list and grafana links.

op-bot: incident created: INC-2027-1189 — conntrack saturation eastus3 — linked to this thread.

chris: FYI we found some orphaned conntrack entries relating to SYN_RECV from probes — running `conntrack -L | grep SYN_RECV | head` shows thousands. That indicates packets being stalled, possibly due to MTU/fragment drops.

sara: I’ll gate the prefetch job and stagger shards across minutes instead of simultaneous starts. PR incoming in 15m.

maria: After canary DaemonSet applied to 2 nodes, connection drops have subsided on those nodes. Rolling to remaining nodes now. Monitoring for regressions. :thumbsup:

devin: Follow-ups for postmortem: root cause (combination of increased short-lived east-west connections + MTU mismatch from RDMA/jumbo frames) and remediation (conntrack tuning, CNI MTU correction, prefetch throttling, consider eBPF).

alex: I'll file a runbook doc with commands we used and safe knobs to tweak (and memory impact notes).

maria: Thanks team. Keeping thread open until all nodes green.

chris: All nodes reporting nf_conntrack_count < 30% after roll. Marking mitigation success for now.

maria: Closing incident in 30m if no flares.
